To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the muon energy spectrum in the range 0.3-1 TeV is compatible with the predictions of QCD-based models of the primary cosmic ray spectrum.

the muon energy spectrum in the energy range from 10 to 200 GeV is well described by the Gaisser-Hillas parametrization with the following values of parameters: the muon energy scale parameter is 0.95 ± 0.05, the muon spectral index is 3.7 ± 0.2 and the muon generation scale height is 60 ± 5 g/cm ^{2}.
the energy spectrum of muons measured with the liquid argon calorimeter BARS is compatible with the predictions of the QGSJetII-03 hadronic model for the energy range 1 TeV < E μ < 10 TeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of muon energy spectra at the energies above 10 14 eV, which is important for understanding the nature of primary cosmic rays.
the development of a large-scale liquid-argon detector for the investigation of the energy spectrum of cosmic muons.
the search for a new physics beyond the Standard Model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BARS is a good instrument for muon energy spectrum measurements.
the BARS experiment is a very promising tool for the measurement of the atmospheric muon energy spectrum in a wide range of energy.

the BARS data are consistent with the hypothesis that the muon energy spectrum at sea level is produced by π, K -decay, but the data cannot be explained without a substantial modification of the existing theoretical models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BARS data is in agreement with the Monte Carlo simulation for the atmospheric muon energy spectrum in the energy range 10-100 GeV.
the muon spectrum is well described by the Gaisser-Hillas parametrization, and the slope parameter is equal to 3.0±0.1.
we have shown the feasibility of the method and the possibility to measure the muon energy spectrum at sea level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liquid-argon technique is suitable for the study of the energy spectrum of atmospheric muons.
the BARS detector has demonstrated a high efficiency for the selection of multiple muon events, which are used for the measurement of the muon energy spectrum.
the liquid-argon calorimeter can serve as a powerful instrument for the studies of the muon energy spectrum.
